page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core operations, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The Intel Xeon processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) support high-throughput mathematical operations, reflected in top-tier scores for CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Single-core performance, however, falls into the average to strong categories, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully exploit this hardware. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only cached small block speeds exceeding 10,000 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds reaching 393.15 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage paired with a 50 Gbps network baseline supports data-intensive operations. In benchmark testing, the instance achieved top-tier results in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and database operations. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. This profile makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded database hosting, large-scale software compilation, real-time image and text processing, and localized machine learning inference tasks that do not require GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory read bandwidth, and exceptional database operation throughput, though single-core performance remains average. With hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512, this instance is optimized for highly parallelized workloads, including software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
